sentences.text:
HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  NC: 2023:KHC:40741  WP No. 45570 of 2015  ORDER 1.

The petitioners are before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:
1. To issue a writ of certiorari quashing the impugned order No.Na Aa E 125 My Aa Pra 2013 Bangalore dated 21.08.2014 at Annexure-C issued by the Respondent No.1.
2. Issue a writ of mandamus directing the 3rd Respondent to issue No Objection Certificate in favour of the Petitioner so as to permit him to utilize the land bearing No. Sy.No.318/1 & 318/2 earlier a part of (Sy.No.318) measuring 1 Acre of land situated at Karnangeri Village, Madikeri Taluk, Kodagu District for residential purposes.
3. To issue any other writ, order or direction as may be deemed fit in the facts and circumstances of the case in the interest of justice.
2. The petitioners claim to be the owner of the agricultural property bearing Sy.Nos.318/1 and 318/2 measuring 1 acre situated at Karnangeri Village, Madikeri Taluk, Kodagu District.
The said land of the petitioners had been demarcated for use as open space/park in the Provisional Master Plan.

The petitioners having wanted to develop the said property on account of the demarcation having lapsed in terms of sub-section (2) of Section 69 of NC: 2023:KHC:40741 the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961 (for short, 'KTCP Act') made an application on 19.09.2022 for issuance of NOC/endorsement to make use of the land for residential purposes.

entities.text: Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: However, no action was taken thereon.

It is in that background that the petitioners are before this Court seeking for a certiorari to be issued to quash the demarcation made in the Provisional Master Plan and for a mandamus as aforestated.

3. On respondents No.3 and 4 having entered appearance, counsel for respondents No.3 and 4 was called upon to make submissions as to whether the requirement under sub-Section (1) of Section 69 of the KTCP Act has been followed and the land of the petitioners have been acquired in terms of the demarcation made.
4. Sri.R.Nagendra Naik, learned counsel for respondents No.3 and 4 submits that there is no such acquisition NC: 2023:KHC:40741 made.

However, since there is a demarcation/reservation made,
NOC has not been issued.

sentences.text: 5. Heard Sri.B.Ravindra Prasad, learned counsel for the petitioners, Smt.Sarita Kulkarni, learned HCGP for respondents No.1 and 2 and Sri.R.Nagendra Naik, learned counsel for respondents No.3 and 4 and perused the papers.

6. Section 69 of the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961 is reproduced hereunder for easy reference:-
69. Acquisition of land designated for certain purposes in a Master Plan.-(1) The Planning Authority may acquire any land designated in a Master Plan for public purposes by agreement or under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Central Act 30 of 2013) as in force in the state.
Explanation: For the purpose of this Section land "designated for public purpose" means designated for the purpose of providing parks, open spaces, public or semi public utilities and infrastructure relating to transport.

sentences.text: (2) If the land designated for public purpose, as under sub-section (1), except land designated for the NC: 2023:KHC:40741 purpose in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of Section 12, is not acquired by agreement within five years from the date of publication of the Master Plan under sub- section (4) of Section nor the proceedings under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Central Act 30 of 2013) are commenced within period of five years, the designated shall be deemed to have lapsed.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: (3) When the designated land use lapses under sub- section (2), the Authority may consider the new land use sought by the landowner of such land, based on the surrounding developments, in the meeting of the Authority, after previous publication in one or more daily newspapers of which at least one shall be in local language having wide circulation in the area and call for objections and suggestions in this regard.

(4) The planning authority shall after considering the proposals to assign land uses and objects and suggestions received in that behalf in the meeting of the Authority, the Authority may convey the assignment of new land use to the owner or reject the proposal for the reasons recorded therein)
7.

Whenever any demarcation/reservation is made in development plan insofar as park/open space are concerned, the Planning Authority is required to implement such demarcation/reservation within a period of 5 years from such demarcation or CDP/RMP coming into force.

In the present case, the Provisional Development Plan having come into force NC: 2023:KHC:40741 on 21.08.2014, the acquisition in terms of sub- Section (1) of Section 69 of KTCP Act ought to be made on or before 20.08.2019 which has not been done.

Subsequent thereto, demarcation/reservation having lapsed, the petitioners are entitled to the benefit of sub-Section (3) of Section 69 of KTCP Act to seek for change of land use from what has been designated in the Provisional Master Plan to that which the petitioners are entitled to seek for which shall be considered in accordance with law without reference to the demarcation/reservation made in the Provisional Development Plan.
Hence, I pass the following:

sentences.text: The Writ Petition is partly allowed.

ii. There is no requirement for certiorari to be issued quashing the Provisional Master Plan dated 21.08.2014 at Annexure-C insofar as petitioners' land is concerned since the said reservation has lapsed in terms of sub-section (2) of Section 69 of KTCP Act.

The petitioners are reserved liberty to file necessary application for change of land use which shall be considered by respondent No.3 without reference to the reservation made earlier in the year 2014 and in accordance with the benefit now conferred on the petitioners in terms of sub-section (3) of Section 69 of KTCP Act.
iv. The learned counsel for petitioners submits that the petitioners would make an online application for change of such land use within 15 days from today.
v. If needful is done, the authorities to consider the said application within 90 days in terms of KTCP Act.
